newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end up mirroring the Dow, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end up mirroring the Dow, seen firm.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended stronger on Monday, tracking the Dow Industrials which rose to its second record closing high, and are expected to continue firm Tuesday, brokers said.
"Considering today's close, we can see the market moving higher tomorrow," a trader said, noting the bourses resisted selling pressure from players who took profits during the session.
Powered by benchmark Telebras preferred, which climbed 1.19 percent, the Bovespa index closed up 1.08 percent at 65,343 points.
Telebras preferred ended at 80.70 reais, while its common stock rose 1.86 percent to 65.89 reais.
Shares of the power sector also posted significant gains. State power utility Eletrobras preferred climbed 3.87 percent to 295 reais, giving continuity to a movement begun last Friday.

The company's stock rose on the back of news that the selloff of Eletrobras' major assets will begin by the end of 1997 and the firm's minority holders will be allowed to swap their stakes in the holding for shares of the privatized units.
Other major gainer was Sao Paulo state's power utility Cesp, whose preferred share jumped 2.32 percent to 31.30 reais. Its common stock rose 1.86 percent to end at 32.80 reais.
The Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index (IEE), comprising the nine most traded stocks of the sector, closed up 1.09 percent at 1,626 points.
Traders only expressed some disappointment with the market's moderate turnover. The Sao Paulo bourse traded $304.2 million.
